evidence_quotes: 27 earthquakes were recorded across Indonesian regions over the 31-day monitoring window — leads immediately with the headline number
One tsunami alert was triggered: a M5.5 shallow-focus quake (depth just 5.4 km) near Tual on 27 January — plain-language explanation of why shallow depth matters
Tobelo dominated activity, accounting for 19 of 27 events (70%) — clear, scannable stat with percentage context
Monitor closely: continued clustering around Tobelo and Tual — compact, no filler
The report has no labeled section headings (e.g., 'Overview', 'Key Events', 'Recommendations') — it is a single bullet list under one title
criticisms: No distinct section headings beyond the title — the entire report is one undifferentiated bullet list, making it hard to navigate by topic (overview vs. notable events vs. recommendations). A non-expert skimming for 'what do I do?' has to read all bullets to find the action item.
The term 'shallow-focus quake' is used without a brief definition; while depth in km is given, 'shallow-focus' is seismological jargon that could confuse a non-specialist.

The final bullet mixes monitoring guidance with technical language ('evolving fault stress', 'aftershock sequences') that may not be immediately clear to a city manager or public information officer without seismology background.
